clue.text: Person in boat making sudden attack

definitions.meaning: in a rowing eight, the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace for the crew
a seizure, as of apoplexy, striking without warning

explanation.surface: A rower aboard a boat suddenly launches an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the rower who sets the rhythm, and a seizure such as apoplexy.

clue.text: Piece of music-slate performance in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the clue wants the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, to knock; a turn is a short act or performance on stage

explanation.surface: A music critic pans a performance heard in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy, night-inspired composition, a genre made famous by Chopin's piano works.

clue.text: Talk about honoured person leading orchestra — a blessing on a wet night!

definitions.text: a blessing on a wet night!

indicators.note: the talk goes around, about, the other pieces, so they sit within it

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: the honoured person comes first, ahead of the orchestra

parts.note: an MBE is a Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
RPO is the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra

explanation.surface: A speech praising a decorated conductor of an orchestra, oddly followed by a remark about rainy nights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: before indoor plumbing, a bedroom pot spared a trip to an outside toilet in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside receptacle for urine saved a cold trip outdoors to the privy, a real mercy in foul weather.

clue.text: European city that falls short of being beautiful

indicators.note: the city is the beautiful word but stops just before its end, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: bonny is a Scottish and northern English word for beautiful

explanation.surface: A city in Europe that is not quite pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city on the Rhine, once the capital of West Germany.

clue.text: Inclined to be involved in sinister manipulation?

definitions.text: Inclined to be involved in sinister manipulation?

parts.words: Inclined to be involved in sinister manipulation?
parts.note: sinister is Latin for the side opposite the right, and manipulation is literally working with the hand, so the clue describes someone favouring that side's hand

explanation.surface: Someone prone to taking part in dark, underhand scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' looks like evil but is its Latin and heraldic sense, the opposite side to dexter; 'manipulation' comes from manus, hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who naturally uses the hand on the sinister side, the one opposite the right, is inclined toward that side.

clue.text: The bonhomie hides what is black

indicators.note: the words the bonhomie conceal the answer across their letters, so it lies within them

explanation.surface: Cheerful good humour conceals something dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for very dark, from the black hardwood ebony.

clue.text: Enlightenment? It maybe found on hill on island

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA; maybe shows this is one example sense
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Perhaps illumination is to be found on a hilltop on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the crossword convention for sex appeal, SA; the question mark flags that enlightenment is meant in its Zen Buddhist sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Zen Buddhism, the sudden awakening or flash of insight a disciple seeks.

clue.text: Like a sort of memory a fellow's got in bank

indicators.note: the fellow has got inside the bank word, splitting it open

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a don is a fellow of a university college; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A man has gone into a bank, perhaps a memory of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a building but is the verb, as in 'bank on' someone. 'Got in' is the container signal; a DON is a university fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer ROM is data that can be retrieved but not altered, a kind of fixed storage chip.

clue.text: Excessively silly host, this person may be good-looking

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: silly suggests the word host is being treated foolishly, its letters jumbled

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself, me

explanation.surface: An overly foolish party host thinks he may be handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' turns HOST into THSO; 'this person' is the setter, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, attractive or appetising in looks, as in a toothsome film star.

clue.text: Daring piece of underwear — tease with kiss denied!

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear

indicators.note: the kiss is refused, so its letter is taken out of the tease word

parts.note: to vex is to annoy or tease
X is the conventional symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A bold lingerie choice, and a flirt refused a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Denied' removes X (a kiss) from VEX, leaving VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and fearless; a synonym for courageous.

clue.text: Fragrant oil placed by chap's seat

parts.note: otto, also attar, is a fragrant oil from rose petals
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Scented oil is set beside a man's chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A low upholstered footstool or couch without back or arms, named after the Turkish empire.

clue.text: Danced a bit having gone crazy inside

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the little-bit word

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, a bit

indicators.note: crazy suggests the word gone is deranged, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone danced a little after losing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges the word gone; 'inside' sets that jumble within the little-bit word. 'Danced' is the past tense, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Performed a South American ballroom step, the past tense of a dance verb.

clue.text: Sin admitted by naughtier rector

indicators.note: the words naughtier rector let in, contain, the answer across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A rather naughty clergyman confesses to wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to go astray or do wrong, as in to stray from what is right.

clue.text: Form of surrender — abandoned custom

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, one left behind or abandoned
a tradition is a custom handed down

explanation.surface: A kind of giving-up: an old habit dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The handing over of a suspect by one country to another for trial, a legal surrender.

clue.text: Milk supplier has a smart job that will help us enjoy a cuppa

definitions.text: job that will help us enjoy a cuppa

parts.note: a teat is a nipple that supplies milk
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A dairy cow gets a smart job helping us enjoy our tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective (clever) but is the noun or verb for a sharp pain, STING. A 'cuppa' is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional sampling of brews to judge blends, which ensures the drink we buy is good.

clue.text: Region well above earth's surface, poison being dissipated in this place

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters of poison are dispersed and regrouped

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: Poison is being spread through the upper atmosphere at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ionised layer of the upper atmosphere, roughly 60 to 1,000 km up, which reflects radio waves.

clue.text: Inexpensive and tacky pad -tenancy has to be renegotiated

indicators.note: renegotiated terms are rearranged, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tatty, low-rent flat whose lease must be agreed afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' is slang for a flat. 'To be renegotiated' shuffles PAD, TENANCY and HAS into the three-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A set phrase for goods that are low-priced and of poor quality.

clue.text: One sits in rickety cottage to think

indicators.note: the one is seated inside the shaky cottage, placed within it
rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters of cottage are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone sits in a ramshackle cottage to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' turns COTTAGE into COGTATE; 'sits in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect at length, a formal synonym.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
Trying out fish after porridge

indicators.note: the fish comes after the porridge, so it is placed second

parts.note: samp is coarsely ground maize porridge, eaten in southern Africa and the US
ling is a fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: Testing a fish course served after the breakfast oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing or tasting a little of something, as with a free taster.

clue.text: Big animals stand in a gap looking wild

indicators.note: the phrase stand in a gap is treated as unruly, its letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Large beasts stand in an opening, looking fierce.
explanation.definitionFit: Large black-and-white bears of China, certainly sizeable creatures.

clue.text: A feature of Hampton Court has daughter gobsmacked

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace, near London, has a famous hedge maze

explanation.surface: A daughter is astonished by a sight at Hampton Court.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMPTON COURT is a Tudor palace near London known for its hedge maze. 'Gobsmacked' is British slang for astounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean utterly astonished.

clue.text: River journeys to the west — get something waterproof?

indicators.note: in an across clue, travelling west means reading right to left, so the river's name runs backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Boats head west on a river; take a raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC is short for mackintosh, a British raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for mackintosh, a rubberised raincoat.

clue.text: Red is interrupting formal occasion half way through

indicators.note: is breaks into the shortened occasion word, sitting within it
the occasion is cut off at its midpoint, leaving only its first half

parts.note: a ceremony is a formal occasion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A red-faced guest interrupts a formal ceremony halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' sits at the front looking like part of the picture but is the definition. 'Half way through' keeps only the first half of the ceremony; 'interrupting' puts 'is' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright cherry-red colour, from the French for cherry.

clue.text: Become friendlier, what?

parts.note: the answer read as instructions says to jumble the first word's letters, out acting as the anagram signal, which produces the clue's word what

explanation.surface: Someone asks 'what?' when told to warm up socially.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat the answer as wordplay, with 'out' meaning rearrange, and it yields the clue's 'what'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's coldness and reserve, like ice melting, and become more relaxed.

clue.text: Scraps thrown out by Socrates regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of Socrates is taken, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Socrates routinely throws out leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for leftover bits of food, remnants of a meal.

clue.text: Student wants central heating in old-fashioned upper room

indicators.note: the heating goes inside the upper room, placed within it

parts.note: a solar is an upper chamber in a medieval house
CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: A student wants heating installed in an old-fashioned attic room.
explanation.walkthrough: A SOLAR is a medieval upper living room; CH is how British property adverts shorten central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person, or one holding a scholarship, so a student.

clue.text: Thick fog? Dash-prisoner has escaped!

indicators.note: the prisoner breaks out, so his letters leave the dash word

parts.note: a soupcon is a dash or tiny amount, as of seasoning
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: In a thick fog, a convict makes a dash for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' seems to be a run but is a small quantity, SOUPCON (soupçon). A 'pea-souper' is a thick London fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a dense fog is pea soup, hence the question mark.

clue.text: River beginning to rise, flooding part of camp

indicators.note: the rising water spreads into the camp piece, so its letter goes inside

parts.note: a tent is one part of a campsite

indicators.note: the start of the word rise, just its first letter

explanation.surface: A river starts to rise, flooding part of a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: The TRENT is a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A major English river flowing through Nottingham to the Humber.

clue.text: Tiny things in our tennis shown to be wrong

indicators.note: being wrong means our tennis is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our tennis game is exposed as flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly massless subatomic particles, about the smallest things known.
